source_review.notes: Checked thirteen primary sources: current Apache Kafka rebalance, consumer/group configuration, distribution, Consumer/RebalanceListener API, and operations documentation; current Apache Flink Kafka and Dynamic Kafka sources; Apache Pulsar subscription documentation; AWS Kinesis lease/shard synchronization; and Google Pub/Sub exactly-once and ordering contracts. All cited URLs returned HTTP 200. System-specific assignment/delivery behavior is attributed rather than generalized.

evidence: Reviewed assignment A_g(p), source bounds L_p/H_p, checkpoint C_p, safe processed P_p, fetch F_p, and arrival/service rates lambda_p/mu_p.
Checked group, subscription, member, generation, lease, partition/split, checkpoint, record identity, and sink fencing remain distinct.
Checked next-position and half-open conventions, MB/s versus GB/hour, record/position spans, and member/partition counts are explicit.
notation_and_syntax.notes: All frontier comparisons are partition-local and generation-qualified; lag arithmetic is not mislabeled as exact record cardinality.

evidence: Executed partition-assignment-frontier with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced assignments m0:[0], m1:[1,4], m2:[2,3,5], equal load 90, completed maximum 104, safe next 102, and unsafe next 105.
Recomputed compact example round-robin loads 120/90/60 versus load-aware 90/90/90 and hot-partition backlog growth 30 units/s.
Recomputed examples: 130-100=30 MB/s = 108 GB/hour; committing fetch 500 over processed 430 risks 70 positions.
Recomputed exercises: balanced 90/90/90/90 versus round-robin 120/100/80/60; frontier spans 1000/920/750/170/80; safe next sequence 202,205,207.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The assignment fixture is a deterministic greedy heuristic demonstration, not an optimality or production-throughput claim.

evidence: Verified L_p<=C_p<=P_p<=F_p<=H_p under the named ordered buffered-source model and identified conditions requiring richer state.
Checked prefix advancement: repeatedly advance P only while P is completed; max(completed)+1 is unsafe when any lower required position is absent.
Verified backlog derivative is approximately max(0,lambda_p-mu_p) under stable same-unit rates and exclusive ownership parallelism is bounded by min(P,M).
Checked generation fencing closes the gap between coordinator reassignment and a delayed old process that may still execute.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Frontier, queueing, and ownership equations are scoped models; compaction, filters, control records, retries, variable work, and message-level delivery alter interpretation.

evidence: Reviewed zero/more members than partitions, unassigned/empty partitions, hot partition, lambda equal/above/below mu, no lag, retention gap, and bounded input completion.
Reviewed out-of-order completions, poison holes, reorder overflow, prefetched suffix, seek with cached data, pause/resume, commit/checkpoint failure, and effect ambiguity.
Reviewed crash, graceful leave, network-isolated zombie, coordinator failover, heartbeat/poll stalls, static-ID collision, mixed protocols, callback timeout, and stale standby state.
Reviewed dynamic discovery, deletion/recreation, shard split/merge ancestry, pattern authorization, zone/residency constraints, credential rotation, metrics leakage, and lifecycle deletion.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Assignment convergence, exclusive effects, progress safety, ordered delivery, capacity, and governance can fail independently.

evidence: Traced join/assignment generation through state restore, fetch, async completion, prefix advancement, checkpoint/effect, revocation, fencing, and successor replay.
Checked at most one current effect-capable owner through both coordinator assignment and sink/state fencing, including zombie execution.
Checked checkpoints never exceed the contiguous durably completed prefix and restore ignores stale local fetch positions.
Checked resource bounds cover fetch/in-flight/reorder buffers, workers, connections, checkpoints, retries, callback deadlines, restore, and coordination metadata.
invariant_checking.notes: Liveness timeouts authorize reassignment but do not prove process termination; effect fencing or idempotency remains mandatory.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step proof from coordination identity through assignment/fencing, frontier tracking, prefix commit, revocation, balancing, bounds, observation, fault tests, and lifecycle.
Checked the ownership argument: current generation token rejects delayed writes from prior generation even when the old process runs.
Checked the prefix argument: C<=P can replay a completed suffix, whereas C>P can skip the first incomplete required position.

Reviewed counterexamples for consumer-count scaling, count-balanced work, timeout-as-stop, heartbeat-as-progress, fetch-as-process, max-completed commit, pause-as-checkpoint, and offset-commit-as-exactly-once.
proof_review.notes: Partition-exclusive groups, message-shared subscriptions, and shard-lease systems are compared without asserting identical semantics.

evidence: Audited uses of assigned, exclusive, current, fenced, completed, processed, committed, checkpointed, ordered, static, eager, incremental, cooperative, exactly-once, and idempotent.
Confirmed ownership and exactly-once statements include group generation, effect/state boundary, framework/source/sink scope, and failure assumptions.
Confirmed current Kafka/Flink/Pulsar/Kinesis/Pub/Sub features are explicitly attributed and time-sensitive defaults are not universalized.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No coordinator timeout, broker commit, assignment protocol, subscription type, or delivery feature is mislabeled as universal end-to-end correctness.

evidence: Reviewed measures for C/P/F/H frontiers, records/bytes/time lag, arrival/service rates, in-flight/reorder work, retention headroom, and per-partition tails.
Reviewed heartbeat/poll/lease, rebalance reason/duration/movement, restore, pause, throttle, downstream wait, GC, auth, and failure evidence.
Confirmed no universal member count, timeout, fetch size, checkpoint interval, assignment heuristic, movement threshold, reorder bound, or lag objective is prescribed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production choices require measured work distributions, state size, client/protocol versions, topology, recovery objectives, sink semantics, and threat/policy constraints.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed partitioned consumption as coordinated ownership plus progress: coordination domains, assignment versus delivery, generations/fencing, four frontiers, completed prefixes, state/effect commits, revocation/assignment, rebalance protocols, liveness, load-aware capacity, flow control, discovery, observation, security, and testing.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed practical group naming, static identity, revoke/drain/restore, source versus framework checkpoints, async prefix tracking, sink fencing, timeout tuning, skew-aware assignment, pause/resume, topology evolution, lag diagnosis, fault injection, and cleanup. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from ownership identity through safe progress and handoff to scaling, observability, and lifecycle. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover idle consumers, weighted balance, hot backlog, frontier gaps, out-of-order completion, zombie fencing, revocation, liveness, shard ancestry, and test design.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Kafka, Flink, Pulsar, Kinesis, or Pub/Sub maintainer, consumer-coordination/distributed-systems researcher, streaming/runtime/state/sink engineer, SRE/platform/security/privacy specialist, records/legal authority, affected-tenant reviewer, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
